1402. 16. October. 0. �?0. — Heinrich von Rosenberg und sein Sohn Peter verkaufen ihren ganzen Antheil an dem Dorf e Jarmirn den Brüdern Weclin and Gregor von Zippendorf um 120 Schock und zwölf Prager Silbergroschen.

CXCII. Nos Henricus et Petrus filius ipsius utrique de Rosembergh principales actores et venditores teuore presentis littere vniuersis et singulis publice profitemur, quia sana cum deliberacione et salubri prehabito consilio vrgente nos necessitatis articulo vendidi- mus partem nostram totalem ville Yaromyrow, decem sexagenas grossorum argenteorum cum vno grosso aunuatim censuautem, cum omni iurisdictione agris cultis et incultis censibus emendis'honoran- ciis robotis pascuis pratis communitatibus singulisque prouentibus iuribus et pertinenciis ac pleno dominio et libertate ad partem pre- dicte ville et eius incolas spectantibus, sic quod nee pro nobis aut nostris successoribus in eadem villa et eius incolis iam condescensis aliquid iuris relinquimus, sed in toto vendidimus famoso viro Wecz- lyno et Gregorio fratribus de Czypyu et ipsorum heredihus et ad mauus famosorum virorum videlicet Petri de Vzdyeczow Przybiconis et Jeorgii fralrum quondam Nicolay de Elhota vero ef iusto vendi- cionis titulo pro centum et viginti sexagenis ac duodecim grossis grossorum argenteorum monete Pragensis iure hereditario ad haben- dum tenendum regendum possidendum vtifruendum libere et pacifice perpetuis temporibus, prout nosmet et antecessores nostri eundem censum in eadem parte ville hucusque libere et quiete dinoscuntur tenuisse. Et pro eisdem bonis a prefato Weczlyno recepimus omnes predictas paratas pecunias nos Henricus et Petrus antedicti. Eadem igitur bona nos Henricus et Petrus prenominati de. Ros«mbergh atque nos Przybico de Zymuticz protunc castri Chrumpnaw purgrauius et Woytyecho de Kraselow protuuc purgrauius in Meydstain fideius- sores pro ipsis et cum ipsis dominis Henrico et Petro predictis de Rosembergh omnes indiuisa manu fide nostra bona omni sine dolo volentes dictum Weczlynum et Gregorium ac heredes et amicos eorum proscriptos in huiusmodi empcione certos et securos reddere promittimus, a data presencium ad sex annos continue reuolueudos disbrigare et libertare ante omnes orphanos, ante queuis dotalicia, ante rrmnem hominem status cuiuslibet impetentem uel volentem impetere, et fídeliter ipsis sex annis expletis et decursis in primis quatuor temporibus tune venientibus aut finaliter in secundis quatuor tethpori- bus proxime tune sequentibuspredicto Weczlyno et Gregorio aut eorum heredibus et amicis predictis intabulare ad terre tabulas regni Bohe- uiie bonos disbrigatores bonorum eorundem tune statuentes, veluti ius terre Bohemie postulat ut requirit. Si uero, quod absit, eadem bona cum omnibus eorum appendenciis superius expressis disbrigare et libertare aut intabulare negligeremus, extunc de tot et tantis et tam bonis nostris mundis liberis propriis hereditatibus, prout dicta bona se extendunt, etiam et tercia parte plus adaucta diclo Weczlyno et Gre gorio heredibus ac amicis eorum prescriptis condescendere promittimus et debemus omni occasione et contradictione procul motis. In casu autem, si nos in huiusmodi bonorum disbrigacione intabulacione aut aliorum in tercia parte plus valencium bonorum condescensione con- trarii essemus et negligentes, extunc mox et statim duo nostrum, qui primum moniti fuerimus, se per alios non excusantes cum duobus famulis et quatuor equis ingredi tenebimur ciuitatem Chrumpnaw ad honestum ibidem hospitem, qui nobis per predictos deputatus fuerit, prestituri ibidem obstagium debitum et consuetum. Nos vero Hen- ricus et Petrus predicti de Rosenberk, si pro faciendo obstagio moniti fuerimus, tune loco nostri alium famosum clientem in ipsum obstagium poterimus collocare, abinde ipsi nos obstagiantes, qui extiterimus, exituri nullo quoquam super iure, nisi prius omnimode disbrigauerimus intabulauerimus bona eadem omnia supradicta aut in bonis nostris tercia parte plus condescenderimus, veluti per nos superius firmiter et infallibiliter est expressum. Elapsis uero qua- tuordecim diebus a predicto obstagii termino continuis prestito per nos obstagio uel non prestito prefatis per nos nondum expletis, pre dicti potestatem habent plenam, quam eis presentibus damus et 233 concedimus, predictas sortis pecunias cum tercia parte plus pecuni- arum accrescente conquirendi nostrum omnium super dampna inter Christianos uel Judeos nobis tamen semper tamdiu dictum seruanti- bus obstagium, donee per nos prenominatis cucditoribus nostris de predictis omnibus satisfactum fuerit plenarie et in tolo. Eciam et de dampnis omnibus et singulis, que predicti per legaciones itineracio- nes expensas impensas seu per alium quemuis modum ob nostre negligencie incuriam perceperint et se ea percepisse íuramento in cruce sine cespitacione, quod dicitur bez zmatku, asserere presump- serint, satisfacere promittimus in toto. Hoc eciam nutanter expresso et excepto, quod nos Henricus et Petrus prefati de Rosenberk vna cum heredibus et successoribus nostris predictam partem ville Yamyrow, sicut superius est tactum, per nos venditam их speciali et beniuolo consensu Weczlyui et Gregorii prefatorum et heredum ipsorum a data presencium infra sex anuos se continue sequentes cum eadem summa pecuniarum veluti est vendita, reemcre possumus hominis cuiuslibet difficultate qualibet non obstante. Et si quis nostrum medio in tempore diuina permissione mortuus extiterit, vnus aut duo tune mox infra vnum mensem a die obitus illius uel illorum continuum sub pena similis obstagii, ut predicitur, eque probum uel probos habeutem uel habentes nobiscum nos residui statuere spon- demus loco defuneti uel defunctorum ad nos pro fideiussore assu- mentes litteram preseutem infringendo et aliam de nowo huic similem renouando, condicionibus tamen in ea verius obseruatis. Et si quis nostrum contra presentem litteram se uerbo uel facto opposuerit aut aliqua íuramenta prestare voluerit, hoc sit et esse debet in sui ipsius preiudicium, sed non huius littere detrimentum. Et quicunque pre sentem litteram cum bona voluntate et pleno ac libero consensu sepetacti Weozlini habuerit heredumque suorum, eidem ¡us competit omnium premissorum. In quorum omnium testimonium et lirmius roboramentum, ut omnia premissa in singulis suis punctis et clau- sulis rata et firma permaneant, sigilla nostra propria no'stra de certa sciencia prest util us sunt appensa. Sub anno domioi millesimo qua- dringentesimo secundo feria secunda die sancti Galli venerabilis confessons. CIV) hier angehängt, oder nin völlig gleiches geführt. c) Siehe CLXXXVII I b. d) Schild mit dem Vordertheil eines Pferdes, darüber ein Helm mit dem Schil deszeichen zur Zierde. — S . Woyty . . . . entries.english:
On 16 October 1402. — Heinrich von Rosenberg and his son Peter sell their entire share in the village of Jarmirn to the brothers Weclin and Gregor von Zippendorf for 120 Schock and twelve Prague silver groschen.

CXCII. We, Henricus and Petrus, his son, both of Rosenberg, principal parties and sellers, publicly declare to all and each by the tenor of this present letter that, after sound deliberation and good counsel, compelled by the pressure of necessity, we have sold our entire share in the village of Yaromyrow, with its annual rent of ten sexagenae of silver groschen and one groschen, together with all jurisdiction, cultivated and uncultivated fields, rents, dues, services, pastures, meadows, commons, all revenues, rights, and appurtenances, and full lordship and liberty belonging to the aforesaid share of the village and its inhabitants. Thus neither for ourselves nor our successors do we retain any right in that village or its inhabitants, to whom the said share has now been transferred; rather, we have sold it in its entirety to the worthy men Weczlyn and Gregor, brothers of Czypyu, and their heirs, and into the hands of the worthy men Peter de Vzdyeczow Przybiconis and Jeorgius, brothers, formerly of Nicolay de Elhota, by a true and lawful title of sale, for 120 sexagenae and twelve groschen of silver groschen of Prague currency, to have, hold, govern, possess, use, and enjoy freely and peacefully in perpetuity by hereditary right, just as we ourselves and our predecessors are known to have held that rent freely and quietly in that part of the village until now. And we, the aforesaid Henricus and Petrus, have received from the aforementioned Weczlyn all the money stated above, ready to hand, for the same property.

Therefore we, Henricus and Petrus aforesaid of Rosenbergh, together with Przybico de Zymuticz, then burgrave of Chrumpnaw Castle, and Woytyecho de Kraselow, then burgrave at Meydstain, as sureties for them and with them, all with undivided faith and without deceit, wishing to make the aforesaid Weczlyn and Gregor and their named heirs and friends secure and safe in this purchase, promise to clear and free the said property from every claimant for six consecutive years from the date of this letter—before all orphans, before every dowry, and before any person of whatever status who makes or wishes to make a claim—and, faithfully, when those six years have expired, within the first four court terms then ensuing, or finally within the next four terms thereafter, to enter it for the aforesaid Weczlyn and Gregor, or their aforesaid heirs and friends, in the land registers of the Kingdom of Bohemia, then appointing good warrantors for those properties as the law of the land of Bohemia requires.

If, God forbid, we neglect to clear and free the property with all its appurtenances stated above, or to enter it in the register, then we promise and are bound to transfer to the said Weczlyn and Gregor, their heirs and friends, as many and such good, clear, free, and hereditary properties of our own as equal the extent of the said property, increased by a third part, all excuses and objections being set aside. If, however, we should oppose or neglect such clearing, registration, or transfer of other property worth a third more, then at once two of us who are first summoned, without excusing themselves through the others, shall be bound to enter the city of Chrumpnaw with two servants and four horses, to provide there the customary and proper surety-hostage at an honourable host designated for us by the aforesaid parties. We, the aforesaid Henricus and Petrus of Rosenberk, if summoned to provide that hostage, may put another worthy man in our place. Those of us who have become hostages shall not leave there on any pretext until we have fully cleared and registered all the aforesaid property or transferred property worth a third more, as firmly and irrevocably set out above.

After fourteen consecutive days from the stated term for the hostage, whether or not we have provided it, if the aforesaid obligations have still not been fulfilled by us, the named parties shall have full power, which we hereby grant, to recover from all of us the principal sum with an additional third in money, by seeking damages among Christians or Jews, while we shall continue to serve the stated hostage for as long as necessary until we have fully satisfied our aforesaid creditors in all these matters. We further promise to compensate in full for all and every loss they may suffer through embassies, journeys, expenses, outlays, or any other means through our negligence, if they assert under oath on the Cross, without hesitation (which is called “bez zmatku”), that they incurred those losses.

This is also expressly stated and excepted: we, the aforesaid Henricus and Petrus of Rosenberk, together with our heirs and successors, may, with the special and willing consent of the aforesaid Weczlyn and Gregor and their heirs, repurchase the share of the village of Yamyrow sold by us, as stated above, within six consecutive years from the date of this letter, for the same sum of money for which it was sold, notwithstanding any difficulty raised by anyone.

And if any of us should die in the meantime by divine permission, the one or two of us who remain shall, within one month continuously from the day of his or their death, under the penalty of a like hostage as aforesaid, provide in his or their place one or more equally worthy men to reside with us, and take them on as surety in place of the deceased, cancelling this letter and renewing another like it, while more faithfully observing its conditions. If any of us opposes this present letter by word or deed or wishes to make any oath, this shall be to his own prejudice and shall not invalidate this letter. Whoever holds this letter with the good will and full and free consent of the aforementioned Weczlyn and his heirs shall have the right to all the foregoing.

In witness and firmer confirmation of all these matters, so that each point and clause remains valid and firm, our own seals have been appended with our certain knowledge. In the year of the Lord 1402, on Monday, the day of St Gall, venerable confessor.

Four small seals, hanging from parchment strips, partly poorly impressed. Seals a and b are in red wax, c and d in white wax.
a) The well-known seal of Heinrich von Rosenberg.
b) This younger Peter von Rosenberg either attached here the small seal of the elder Peter (compare CIV), or used one entirely like it.
c) See CLXXXVII I b.
d) Shield with the forepart of a horse, above it a helmet decorated with the shield's charge. — S. Woyty… De… Kraselow.
